q: Why did my sales drop yesterday?

checks.what: tool: measures the change with compare_period

answer:
Sales did not drop — net sales on 2026-10-13 were ₹91,220 (up 127.3% vs 2026-10-12), so the premise is incorrect; yesterday was a stronger day and sits well within the normal range for this metric. 

Evidence
- Net sales: 2026-10-12 = ₹40,119 → 2026-10-13 = ₹91,220 (+127.3%).
- Orders: 26 → 45 (+73.1%); Net AOV: ₹1,543 → ₹2,027 (+31.3%) — both rose and together explain the higher sales.
- Refund / refunded amount: ₹11,340 → ₹32,464 (+186.3%) — larger refunds that day but still within its normal range and not identified as a causal driver.
- Ad spend: ₹38,661 → ₹50,440 (+30.5%) — moved with sessions; the analysis found correlation but no supported causal link.

What this means (short)
- The apparent “drop” is not present in the data — sales increased because both order volume and average order value rose.
- The diagnostics found no single supported cause for unusual movement; refunds and ad spend rose but were within normal variation and were not proven as causes.

Period: 2026-10-13 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-14
